title: Meller Holds On as Mullin Breaks the Course Record
title_candidates: Meller Holds On as Mullin Breaks the Record
A Record Falls, A Trophy Nearly Slips
Praia D'El Rey's Day of Records and Near-Misses
theme: The final round produced history at the top of the card and just short of it everywhere else — a new course record, a near-miss Trophy fightback, and business as usual at the foot of the table.
tone: wry, warm, needling, faithful to the numbers
opening_hook: Praia D'El Rey had hosted TEG golf only once before, and its second visit produced a new course record, two career-best charges that both ran out of holes at exactly the same distance from the lead, and a Wooden Spoon delivered with the tidy inevitability of a man who has never once threatened to escape it.

round_story.subject: David Mullin's course-record 83 at Praia D'El Rey
round_story.why_it_matters: It is the best individual round of the entire week: a new Praia D'El Rey course record, the 2nd-best gross round in TEG history to date, and only the 2nd-best net round of Mullin's own 23-round career — all produced on the tournament's final day.
round_story.shape: Mullin goes bogey-free from the 4th to the 8th, then stumbles with a triple bogey at the 10th that threatens to derail the round entirely. He answers immediately with a birdie at the 11th, holds the card together through the 13th, and closes out a new course record of 83 gross — beating the previous mark by a shot.
headline_candidates: A New Best at Praia D'El Rey
round_story.standfirst: A triple bogey at the 10th barely dented a round that turned out to be the best gross card played all week.

race_story.subject: Henry Meller survives a late Trophy scare
race_story.why_it_matters: This is the final round, so the Trophy, Green Jacket and Wooden Spoon are all settled here: Henry Meller's 15-shot cushion shrank alarmingly before holding, while David Mullin and Alex Baker both confirmed leads they had built well before this round.
race_story.shape: Meller starts the day 15 clear in the Trophy but posts the joint-worst round in the top half of the field, while Gregg Williams and Stuart Neumann both fire career-best net rounds of -12 to haul the gap down into single figures. It is not quite enough — Meller's cushion holds at 7 — while David Mullin's Green Jacket lead balloons to 15 and Alex Baker's Wooden Spoon is confirmed by 8.
race_story.standfirst: Gregg Williams and Stuart Neumann both closed with the best net rounds of their careers, but Henry Meller's early-week cushion proved just enough to see out the TEG 7 Trophy.

discovered_storylines.subject: Jon Baker's back-to-back blow-ups at the 10th and 11th
discovered_storylines.why_it_matters: Jon Baker was joint-second in the Trophy and leading the Green Jacket after round one; a sextuple bogey immediately followed by a quadruple bogey in this final round completed a slide to 5th and 4th respectively, the biggest fade in the field.
discovered_storylines.shape: Baker plays a tidy, bogey-free stretch from the 2nd to the 5th, suggesting a strong finish to the week. Instead he runs up an 11 at the 10th and a 7 at the very next hole, and the tournament's early pace-setter finishes fifth in the Trophy and fourth in the Green Jacket.
headline_candidates: Baker Fades From First to Fourth
discovered_storylines.standfirst: A sextuple bogey and a quadruple bogey in successive holes capped a slow-motion slide from early pace-setter to also-ran.

discovered_storylines.subject: Alex Baker's chaotic final round confirms the Wooden Spoon
discovered_storylines.why_it_matters: Two more quintuple bogeys in the final round, either side of a rare hot patch, capped a tournament in which Alex Baker was bottom half in all four rounds and never came close to escaping the Wooden Spoon.
discovered_storylines.shape: Baker opens with a quadruple bogey at the 3rd and a quintuple at the 6th, briefly rallies with a birdie-fuelled run from the 13th to the 15th, then runs up a second quintuple bogey at the 16th. He finishes the tournament 8 shots clear of Jon Baker at the bottom of the table.
headline_candidates: Alex Baker Wraps Up the Spoon
Alex Baker's Spoon Was Never in Doubt
discovered_storylines.chosen_headline: Alex Baker Wraps Up the Spoon
discovered_storylines.standfirst: Two quintuple bogeys either side of a rare purple patch summed up a tournament Alex Baker's Wooden Spoon was never really in danger of leaving.

race_state_note: No lead changed hands in any of the three competitions this round — Henry Meller's Trophy cushion merely narrowed while David Mullin's Green Jacket advantage widened to its largest margin of the tournament.
